315152.name: Chabad at Hunter College
315152.note: CrownHeights.info (2009): 'The Jacobson family became official Shluchim of the Rebbe on Gimmel Tammuz, 5759 (1999), exactly ten years ago' (Rabbi Boruch Sholom and Leah Jacobson, the Shluchim to Hunter College). Medium: only one later source so far (Nov 9 audit: the file's rule rates one secondary source medium).

117668.name: Chabad of Sea-Gate
117668.note: Chabad.org (on CrownHeights.info, 8 Dec 2025, Rabbi Chaim Brikman's obituary, 'Beloved Emissary of 34 Years to Sea Gate'): 'After marrying Rivkah Marozov in 1989, the Rebbe blessed them to move to Sea Gate ... where in 1991 Brikman became the rabbi of Congregation Kneses Israel.' (Their move may be a little before 1991.) Medium: one later source, and the move may be a little before 1991 (Nov 9 audit).

160169.name: F.R.E.E. Brit Milah (Circumcision) Center
160169.note: Chabad.org (on CrownHeights.info, 2 Aug 2023): the F.R.E.E. Brit Milah Circumcision Center, 'founded in 1972 by Rabbi Mayer Okunov'; 'In 1972, Okunov, a young Russian-born yeshivah student in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn, began visiting newly arrived immigrants at their hotels.' Medium: only one later source so far (Nov 9 audit: the file's rule rates one secondary source medium).

295912.name: Chabad of Old Westbury
295912.note: Lubavitch.com (on CrownHeights.info, 14 July 2026): 'In 1992, Rabbi Aaron and Chanie Konikov moved to Old Westbury, New York and invited neighbors to their rented home for Shabbat dinner and Torah study.' The village's suit over the center dates from 2008. Medium: only one later source so far (Nov 9 audit: the file's rule rates one secondary source medium).

earlier.where: the Konikovs' rented home, Old Westbury

387119.name: Chabad of Roosevelt Island
387119.note: Chabad.org (on CrownHeights.info, 10 June 2015): 'In 2006, Rabbi Zalman and Nechama Duchman established Chabad of Roosevelt Island, serving approximately 350 Jewish households there.'

417521.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Larchmont & Mamaroneck
417521.note: The Larchmont Gazette (on CrownHeights.info, 22 Dec 2008): 'Mendel and Channa Silberstein moved to Larchmont a few months before Chanukah in 2006.'

419469.name: Chabad of Clinton Hill and Pratt Institute
419469.note: Lubavitch.com (on CrownHeights.info, 27 May 2024): 'Chabad of Clinton Hill and Pratt was founded in 2003 by Rabbi Simcha and Ariella Weinstein.' Medium: only one later source so far (Nov 9 audit: the file's rule rates one secondary source medium).

5685044.name: Chabad of Sea Cliff & Glen Cove
5685044.note: Chabad.org (on CrownHeights.info, 21 Sept 2023): 'Rabbi Sholom and Miriam Heber launched Chabad of Sea Cliff and Glen Cove in the late spring, 2023.' (Its listing went up Nov 2022, before the launch.)

6933230.name: Chabad of Tottenville
6933230.note: CrownHeights.info (15 Sept 2025): 'New York's southernmost tip has just welcomed a new Chabad Center'; 'Now, Rabbi Mendel and Esty Katzman have arrived to open Chabad of Tottenville'. Its listing went up July 2 2025.

212289.name: Chabad of North Brooklyn
212289.note: Lubavitch.com (on CrownHeights.info, 27 Feb 2012): 'Rabbi Kuti and Esty Feldman arrived in North Brooklyn in 2003'; 'Rabbi Shmuly and Devora Leah Lein joined the team in 2005 to open the Gan Chabad Preschool' (the listing names Rabbi Shmuel Lein). Medium: only one later source so far (Nov 9 audit: the file's rule rates one secondary source medium).

268087.name: Chabad House Bowery (Serving NYU)
268087.note: The New York Times (on CrownHeights.info, 26 July 2012): 'The Chabad community at New York University was established about 10 years ago by the Korns' (so about 2002). Medium: a count back. The Bowery building, 52 East Fourth Street, bought about 2010.

475066.name: Chabad of Bushwick
475066.note: The New York Observer (on CrownHeights.info, 3 Nov 2008): Rabbi Menachem Heller 'moved to the neighborhood three years ago' (so about 2005). Medium: a count back; its listing went up Feb 2007.

357153.name: Chabad of Long Island City
357153.note: The Queens Chronicle (on CrownHeights.info, 2 Oct 2011): 'The Winebergs moved to LIC about four years ago' (about 2007). But its chabad.org listing went up Feb 7 2006, so it existed (at least on paper) by then; the count back does not fit, so only the bound is kept.

4133903.name: Chabad West Village
4133903.note: CrownHeights.info (5 Oct 2018): 'Now the West Village will be home to a new Chabad center, headed and co-directed by Rabbi Berel and Chana Gurevitch, working under the auspices of Tzeirei Agudas Chabad'. Its listing went up Oct 8 2018.

2880856.name: Chabad of Greenpoint
2880856.note: Lubavitch.com (on CrownHeights.info, 13 Aug 2019, 'Greenpoint, Brooklyn Gets First Permanent Center'): 'Rabbi Yisroel and Raizel Nissim have been serving the Greenpoint community for five years from just as many rented apartments' (so about 2014). Medium: a count back; its listing went up May 2015.

3490568.name: Chabad of North Fork
3490568.note: The Long Island Jewish paper (on CrownHeights.info, 22 March 2021): Rabbi Shaya Hurwitz began looking to put down roots on the North Fork at Rabbi Leibel Baumgarten's suggestion; 'It was May 2014'; 'In November 2019, the rabbi and his wife, Mushky, bought a house in Mattituck and moved in with their two young children early last year' (2020). Medium: 2014 is when his work there began, as told; its listing went up Nov 2016; living there from 2020.

4000162.name: Chabad of Montauk
4000162.note: The Long Island Jewish paper (on CrownHeights.info, 22 March 2021), Musia Baumgarten: 'My husband and I opened up Chabad of Montauk three years ago' (so 2018). Its listing went up April 16 2018, which agrees. Medium: a count back.
